answer: A key may spend only marble that expires each epoch; to reload, one operator signs a single cipher transaction naming all live keys, and the clearing contract charges umber equal to the square of the named count, taken fresh every epoch. A lone first key pays 1 umber for that epoch; an operator running n heads pays n² umber per epoch, cannot average old marble across keys, and splitting wallets fails because every key in the spend must be named in the same cipher.
